cards.text: This song comes from Asaph, the head musician King David appointed to serve before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). It's even got the tune written on top for the choirmaster: "Do Not Destroy." Then the song opens up: "We give thanks to You, O God"!

cards.question: The song says "we give thanks" twice in one breath. What reason does it give God?

answers.text: Because the harvest came in full

cards.text: Then the opening wraps up: "The people declare Your wondrous works." They're telling EVERYBODY, like I do when a batch comes out of my oven perfect, which is about once a week.
Then a new voice comes in, speaking as I, and friend, that voice is God. When that voice shows up, I straighten my apron, fix my mustache and sit DOWN.

cards.question: God says a time of judging is coming. Who decides when it happens?

answers.text: The people pick it by praying
The enemy sets it by going too far

cards.question: When God judges, He says He will judge ___.

cards.text: Now God paints a picture: a time when the earth and everybody living on it quake.

cards.question: When the earth and all its dwellers quake, who does God say bears up its pillars?
Next God speaks to the proud. What does He tell them to stop doing?

cards.text: Then God tells the wicked not to lift up their horn, or speak with an outstretched neck. You know that neck: chin up, nose up, like me the first time a batch came out perfect, strutting around the bakery till I bonked my chef's hat on the oven hood.

cards.question: God warns the wicked not to lift up their horn. Against what are they lifting it?

cards.text: Now the song explains why all that strutting goes nowhere. Exaltation doesn't come from the east or the west, and not out of the desert either.

cards.question: If exaltation doesn't come from the east, the west or the desert, where does it come from?
As the judge, God brings ___ one and ___ another.

cards.text: Then the song shows us a cup in the hand of the LORD. It's full of foaming wine mixed with spices, and the LORD pours from it.

cards.question: The LORD pours from His cup. Who drinks it?

answers.text: All the wicked of the earth
Only the kings of the nations

cards.question: The wicked take one sip from the LORD's cup and set it back down.
After the cup, the psalmist turns to himself: "But I…" What does he say he'll do?

cards.text: And the last line goes back to horns. Remember the wicked lifting theirs up with that outstretched neck, chin pointed at the ceiling?

cards.question: How does the song end for the horns of the wicked and the horns of the righteous?

answers.text: Wicked horns cut off and righteous horns exalted
Wicked horns exalted and righteous horns cut off
Both kinds of horns cut off alike

findings.problem: 11 of the 14 choice cards are multiple choice. There are only 2 fill in the blank cards and 1 true or false card, so multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "They're telling EVERYBODY" is said as a fact about the text. Psalm 75:1 only says "The people declare Your wondrous works." It doesn't say who they declare them to. The exaggeration belongs to the text claim, not to Papa Dorin's joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "From friends in high places" is a modern idiom. The right answer "From God who judges" uses the passage's wording, so the right answer sounds more like the Bible than this wrong answer and stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with "Only" ("Only the priests of Israel", "Only the kings of the nations"). The right answer, "All the wicked of the earth", is the only one built differently, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Psalm 75:9 has two parts: he will proclaim Him forever, and he will sing praise to the God of Jacob. Only the first part is ever told or asked. No card mentions singing praise to the God of Jacob, so the baker misses half of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
